**Author's Note**
**Why did the Bible not record the full text of all Jesus' sermons and deeds?**

The apostle John offers us an answer as he concludes his Gospel, affirming that if every one of the deeds and teachings of Christ were written down in detail, even the whole world would not have room for the books that would be written (Jn 21:25). He reminded us that the Holy Spirit granted the explicit written record of all that is entirely sufficient for our salvation, faith, and edification (Jn 20:31).

The first and largest portion of this book is a literary and devotional reconstruction of the discourse Jesus may have delivered to the two disciples on the road to Emmaus, as recorded in Luke 24:13-35. The evangelist informs us that Jesus, "beginning with Moses and all the Prophets," explained to the disciples everything concerning himself—the Messiah, the Christ—found in all the Scriptures. The verbatim, word-for-word transcript of that historic sermon was not inscribed upon the pages of the New Testament. Yet the question returns: Why did one of the most sublime exegetical expositions in human history remain preserved only as a summary?

The walk from Jerusalem to Emmaus was approximately 11 kilometers (about seven miles, or sixty stadia, as recorded in Lk 24:13), which would require between two and three hours on foot. Ample time for an extensive and profound exposition of the Scriptures.

We believe that through this apparent omission, the Holy Spirit has extended to each of us a permanent invitation and challenge: to open the Old Testament for ourselves, walk that same hermeneutical road, and seek and discover Christ across every page.

The discourse follows the canonical order of the Hebrew Scriptures: the Torah (Moses), the Former Prophets (Joshua through Kings), the Poetic Writings (Psalms), and the Latter Prophets (Isaiah through Malachi), reflecting the very structure employed by Jesus in Luke 24:44: "Everything must be fulfilled that is written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets and the Psalms."

The references in brackets throughout the text indicate the Old Testament passages cited. In the final endnotes, theological and exegetical comments and observations from the author are arranged, annotating each section of the work following the conclusion of the narrative, so as to maintain the uninterrupted flow of the artistic prose.[EN_REF:1][EN_REF:2]

This work does not intend to "add" anything to the Bible. If this reading causes your heart to burn within you and leads you back to direct engagement with the Holy Scriptures, this book will have achieved its purpose in full.
One more thing! At the very end of the book, on the final page, I have a request and a special surprise for you! I hope you enjoy it!
The peace of the Lord be with you! Happy reading!
**PART I - THE TORAH OF MOSES**

The sun was beginning its slow descent over the Judean hills, casting long golden shadows along the rocky path winding downward from Jerusalem toward the village of Emmaus. Two men walked with weary, heavy steps, their faces downcast and their hearts shattered. They were disciples of the Nazarene.

Only hours earlier they had departed from the clamor of the Holy City, where the savage shouts of Friday still seemed to echo from the limestone walls: *"Crucify him! Crucify him!"*. The Roman cross had crushed their hopes. Three days later, on that very morning, certain women from their company had hurried to the tomb and returned with breathtaking news: the stone was rolled away, his body was gone, and angels proclaimed he was alive. But who could believe such things? They had not seen him.

Though risen, no one had yet recognized him immediately, not even his closest followers. Frustrated expectations, lack of faith, and crushing disappointment caused his features in their eyes to appear altered, or their eyes to be "kept from" associating him with the broken, crucified man of three days before.

Jesus drew near to Cleopas and young Nathaniel, two disciples who, leaving Jerusalem, were traveling toward the village of Emmaus. He began to converse with them. His voice carried the gentle authority and profound clarity of One who knows every word of the Scriptures and the deepest depths of the human soul.[EN_REF:3][EN_REF:4]
Jesus asked them:
"What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?"
They stood still, their faces etched with sadness. Cleopas, one of the disciples, answered him:
"Are you the only one visiting Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?"
"What things?" Jesus asked.

"About Jesus of Nazareth," they replied. "He was a prophet, powerful in word and deed before God and all the people. The chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death, and they crucified him; but we had hoped that he was the one who was going to redeem Israel. And what is more, it is the third day since all this took place."
And they continued:

"In addition, some of our women amazed us. They went to the tomb early this morning but didn't find his body. They came and told us that they had even seen a vision of angels, who said he was alive. Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see Jesus."
He said to them:
"How foolish you are, and how slow to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Did not the Messiah have to suffer these things and then enter his glory?"
**1. In the Beginning - The Seed of the Woman (Genesis 3:15)**

The question seemed strangely provocative, coming from a stranger who moments before had seemed entirely unaware of recent events. Yet the gravity of the moment left no room for resentment. The crushing grief of a shattered dream weighed upon the shoulders of Cleopas and his companion, far heavier than the dusty miles remaining before them. Their faces, weathered by the heartbreak of seeing their deepest hope nailed to a Roman cross, were searching for answers that the authorities of Israel could not provide.
Their fellow traveler looked upon them with profound compassion, taking in the turmoil of their souls before unfolding the holy Scriptures.

He drew a little closer, bridging not only the physical distance, but the aching sorrow of their troubled spirits. The Stranger spoke with none of the harsh, arid detachment that so often characterized the debates of the Teachers of the Law; rather, his voice carried the warm, reassuring strength of a shepherd gathering and sheltering frightened sheep.

Looking tenderly once more into the eyes of the two disciples, whose vision was still kept from discovering who he was, Jesus paused briefly, allowing the silence of the road to quiet their anxious minds before uttering his first words:
"Listen closely to me, my friends. You are sorrowful because you believed the Messiah would come to deliver Israel by the sword.
"Yet know this: it was necessary that the Scriptures should first be fulfilled. Your unbelief and slowness to understand what the prophets foretold need not remain. Listen carefully; I will show you.

"In the beginning, when the first man and the first woman fell from fellowship with God, when the ancient serpent seduced them into rebellion—what happened then? The Lord, rather than destroying mankind, pronounced a solemn verdict upon the serpent. And within that very sentence, the earliest promise of redemption was heralded to the world:
*"And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; **he will crush your head**, and you will strike his heel." *[Gn 3:15]**

"Understand this: there, in the garden, before the fallen pair draped in shame, God announced that from the **seed of the woman** One would arise—an offspring—who would crush the serpent's head. Yet to crush it, he himself would be bruised. Victory would come through suffering. Redemption would be born through pain. This is the protoevangelium—the first good news ever proclaimed upon the earth.[EN_REF:5]

"Adam understood. He named his wife **Eve**—*Hawwâ*, meaning *life* or *mother of all the living*—because he believed that life would endure, that the **seed** would come, that through motherhood hope would be born.[EN_REF:6]

"And Eve, when she gave birth to her firstborn son, exclaimed: *"With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man!"* [Gn 4:1]—Eve cried out in eager anticipation, and the Father sealed in patient grace the appointed time for his promise. She did not know that the seed must journey through generations of patriarchs, monarchs, and exiles before the soil was prepared.[EN_REF:7]

"From that hour, friends, all of human history revolves around the story of this seed: who would bear it, how it would be preserved, and when, at long last, the fruit would blossom that would forever crush the head of the ancient serpent."
**2. The Preservation of the Seed - Noah and the Prophecy concerning Shem (Genesis 9:25-27)**
Jesus continued:

"The seed of the woman had to be preserved. Cain, the firstborn, murdered his brother Abel—and in that brutal deed the hostility of the serpent struck against the line of promise. The seed was plunged into peril. Yet the Lord granted Eve another son—Seth—who carried forward the royal lineage, born *'in the likeness of Adam, according to his image'* [Gn 5:3].[EN_REF:8]

"Later, when the wickedness of the human race multiplied across the earth, when *'every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil all the time'* [Gn 6:5], the Lord brought the flood. Yet in the midst of overwhelming judgment, he preserved Noah—a righteous man—and his household. The ark was the vessel by which the seed of the woman was saved, not by human merit, but by the sovereign grace and purpose of the Lord.[EN_REF:9]
"And when the floodwaters receded, Noah prophesied over his sons. Concerning the son named Shem, he declared:
*"Praise be to the LORD, the God of Shem!"* [Gn 9:26]

"Understand: out of all the families of the earth, it was within the tents of Shem that the Lord chose to dwell. The seed of the woman would advance along the line of Shem. Through Shem came the Hebrews, through Shem came Abraham, through Shem came the nation of Israel—and through that sacred line would come the Promised One."
**3. The Promise to Abraham - All Nations Shall Be Blessed (Genesis 12, 15, 17, 22)**
"Then came the great calling. Out of all the descendants of Shem, the Lord singled out an elderly, childless man living in a pagan land, and said to him:

*"Go from your country, your people and your father's household to the land I will show you. I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you."* [Gn 12:1-3]

"Take note: in you—through your seed—all peoples on earth will be blessed. Not Israel alone, but all nations. The seed of Abraham would be the channel through which the blessing of God would pour out to all humanity. This is the promise you have known since childhood.

"And the Lord confirmed this promise when, upon Mount Moriah, Abraham drew the knife over his own son, his only son, Isaac—ready to offer him in sacrifice at God's command. And the Angel of the Lord affirmed:

*"I swear by myself, declares the LORD, that because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son, I will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will take possession of the cities of their enemies, and through your offspring all nations on earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed me."* [Gn 22:16-18]

"Consider carefully that when Abraham placed the son of promise upon the altar, the Lord provided a substitute ram for the sacrifice. One died in place of the other. God spared the son of Abraham by providing a ram caught in a thicket by its horns, but *'God did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all'* [Rm 8:32].[EN_REF:10]

"These events took place on the mountain Abraham called *Yahweh Yireh*, meaning *'The LORD will provide'* [Gn 22:14]. And so it would be: in the very region where that mount stands, between Mount Moriah and the hill of Golgotha outside Jerusalem, centuries later, the true Lamb would be provided—the One who takes away the sin not of one man alone, but of the entire world.
**4. Jacob's Prophecy - Until Shiloh Comes (Genesis 37-50)**

"The lineage narrowed further. From Abraham came Isaac. From Isaac came Jacob. And from Jacob came twelve sons—the twelve tribes of Israel. Yet the seed of promise, the coming Sovereign, would not proceed from all twelve tribes. He would come from one alone.

"When our father Jacob lay on his deathbed in Egypt, he gathered his twelve sons and declared what would happen in days to come, *'in the days to come'* [Gn 49:1]. And of them all, it was to Judah—not to Reuben, the firstborn, nor to Joseph, the beloved—that he addressed this prophecy:

*"Judah, your brothers will praise you; your hand will be on the neck of your enemies; your father's sons will bow down to you. You are a lion's cub, Judah... The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he to whom it belongs shall come (Shiloh) and the obedience of the nations shall be his."* [Gn 49:8-10]

"The scepter—the staff of sovereign rule—would remain with Judah until Shiloh came. And who is Shiloh? He is the rightful possessor of dominion, to whom all nations owe obedience.[EN_REF:11][EN_REF:12]
"And notice what Jacob declared next:
*"He will tether his donkey to a vine, his colt to the choicest branch; he will wash his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes."* [Gn 49:11]
"Garments drenched in wine... robes washed in blood... This speaks not merely of vineyard abundance, my brothers. Therein lies a sacred emblem of a sacrificial future."[EN_REF:13]

"You know that treading grapes in a winepress, with that deep crimson juice splashing across one's clothing, also evokes exhausting toil, conflict, agony, and death. One of the Midianite princes, for example, was slain at a winepress [Jdg 7:25]. The Scriptures even portray the Lord treading the winepress alone, as Isaiah described [Is 63:3].

"Treading grapes is customarily a festive harvest celebration performed together in joy. To tread it entirely alone signifies excruciating, isolated agony. Spiritually, it mirrors the sacrifice of Christ in Gethsemane (meaning literally *'olive press'*) and upon the Cross, where he bore in solitary agony the crushing weight of human iniquity. Yet do not despair, for the outcome of that crushing is everlasting abundance, my friends!
**5. Joseph Prefigures the Coming and Mission of the Messiah (Genesis 37-50)**

"Consider also what was unveiled across generations through another of Jacob's sons: just as Joseph was the beloved son sent by his father to seek his brothers in the fields of Dothan, so Jesus was sent from the Father's bosom to his own brothers according to the flesh. Yet instead of love, he encountered jealousy and conspiracy; he was hated without cause and sold for the price of a slave.

"Joseph was stripped of his fine tunic, cast into a dark pit, and imprisoned unjustly between two transgressors—prefiguring the agony of the Passion of the Son of God, who was stripped bare upon Calvary, counted as a criminal though innocent, and suspended between two outlaws, tasting the darkness of the grave.

"Yet the pit and the dungeon could not hold Joseph. Brought forth from prison, he was elevated to the throne to open the royal storehouses and rescue the world from famine. In the same way, the Father raised his Son from death and exalted him to the highest place, making him the Living Bread who satisfies the eternal hunger of all who believe.

"Do you remember when Joseph revealed himself to his brothers at their second encounter? Weeping with tears of forgiveness, he unveiled the mystery of divine providence: *'You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives'* [Gn 50:20]. In the very same way, the cruelty of Calvary and the malice of men were transformed by the Most High into the supreme decree of world redemption, as the true Passover Lamb!
**6. The Passover Lamb - Redemption by Blood (Exodus 12)**

Still without recognizing the Master, the disciples were astonished by such profound wisdom from the Scriptures, yet they wondered whether suffering alone might have fulfilled the prophecies—whether death was truly necessary, since such an end seemed utterly shameful for his followers.
Then Jesus continued:
"If what I have told you has not yet made it clear, let me explain further, so that your understanding may fully open:

"The seed of the woman, the promised Offspring, was appointed to accomplish a work immeasurably greater than sitting upon an earthly political throne. To comprehend this, recall the first great redemption of our people. Look at Moses in Egypt. On that night of terror, when God's judgment was about to fall upon the land, what did the Lord require of Israel?

*"The animals you choose must be year-old males without defect, and you may take them from the sheep or the goats... Then they are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs... The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you... When the LORD goes through the land to strike down the Egyptians, he will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway, and he will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down."* [Ex 12:5, 7, 13, 23]

"It was not the strength of our fathers' hands nor their own righteousness that spared them from the angel of death. It was the blood of a spotless, unblemished lamb shed in their stead. The Lord passed over—*Pesach*, the Passover—when he saw the crimson mark upon the doorframes.

"Friends, realize that the Messiah came not merely to teach or to conquer, but to be that Lamb. Do you not see the breathtaking precision of God's calendar? He was betrayed, condemned, and crucified at the exact hour when the Passover lambs were being slaughtered in the Temple! He is the true Passover Lamb of the new covenant, and his blood upon the cross is the only mark that delivers us from eternal judgment."[EN_REF:14]
**7. The Substitution of the Firstborn - The Ransom of Life (Exodus 13)**
"And what did the Lord declare immediately following the deliverance from Egypt?
*"Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal."* [Ex 13:2]

"Every firstborn belonged to God, because the lives of the firstborn had been spared in Egypt. Yet the law prescribed that while clean animals were sacrificed, the firstborn sons of men were to be redeemed through the payment of a ransom price, by a substitutionary offering [Ex 13:13-15].

"Here lies the profound mystery of the incarnation and redemption: He who walked among us is the true Firstborn over all creation. He is the only begotten Son of the Father. And he came not to be redeemed with silver or gold, nor with the blood of ordinary lambs. He came, as the unblemished Firstborn, to become the ransom. He gave his life as a ransom for many, so that all who stood condemned to death might be purchased for God."[EN_REF:15]
**8. The Tabernacle and the Day of Atonement - God Dwells with Man (Exodus 25; Leviticus 16)**
"And while the people journeyed through the wilderness, the Lord commanded:
*"Then have them make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell among them."* [Ex 25:8]

"That entire Tabernacle—the bronze altar, the basin, the golden lampstand, the table of showbread, the veil, and the ark of the covenant—every detail was a pattern of heavenly realities, pointing straight to the Messiah. He is the true Tabernacle, the Word made flesh who pitched his tent among us!
"And consider the Day of Atonement—*Yom Kippur*. That solitary day in the year when the high priest entered behind the veil into the Most Holy Place:

*"He is to take some of the bull's blood and with his finger sprinkle it on the front of the atonement cover... In this way he will make atonement for the Most Holy Place because of the uncleanness and rebellion of the Israelites, whatever their sins have been."* [Lv 16:14, 16]

"No man could behold the uncovered glory of God and live. The high priest entered with trembling, veiled in a cloud of incense, and that atonement lasted for only a single year. It had to be repeated year after year, for the blood of bulls and goats can never take away sins permanently.

"Yet what took place three days ago, at the ninth hour, when Christ breathed his last upon the cross? The thick veil of the Temple was torn in two from top to bottom! The Messiah entered not into a sanctuary made by human hands, but into heaven itself. And he entered not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own precious blood, having secured eternal redemption. He is, at once, both the perfect High Priest and the spotless Lamb!"[EN_REF:16]
**9. The Prophet Like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15-19)**

"You revere Moses—and what a mighty servant of God he was! Deliverer, lawgiver, covenant mediator. He stood before Pharaoh and prevailed. He cried out to the Lord and the sea parted. He received the Law upon Sinai. He pleaded for the people when the wrath of God burned against them.
"Yet Moses knew that he was not the final fulfillment. He was a forerunner—a shadow—of the One to come. Therefore he declared to the assembly before his death:
*"The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your fellow Israelites. You must listen to him."* [Dt 18:15]
"And the Lord confirmed those words:
*"I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their fellow Israelites, and I will put my words in his mouth. He will tell them everything I command him."* [Dt 18:18]

"A prophet like Moses: mediator of a greater covenant, deliverer from a bondage far deeper than Egypt, who would speak the very words of the living God. Moses was the temporary deliverer; the One to come would be the everlasting Redeemer.[EN_REF:17]

"And remember: just as Moses lifted up the bronze serpent in the wilderness so that whoever looked upon it was healed [Nm 21:8-9], even so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life."[EN_REF:18]
**10. The Star of Jacob and the Scepter of Israel (Numbers 24:17)**

"Before his departure, Moses recorded the oracle of Balaam—that pagan seer hired to curse Israel, who could speak only blessings because the Spirit of God came upon him. Gazing across the ages, he saw what would happen in the latter days and prophesied:
*"I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob; a scepter will rise out of Israel..."* [Nm 24:17]

"A star: emblem of radiant, heavenly majesty. A scepter: emblem of royal authority and dominion. That foreign pagan seer caught a glimpse of the Messiah of Israel centuries before his arrival."[EN_REF:19]
**PART II - THE FORMER PROPHETS: FROM JOSHUA TO THE THRONE OF DAVID**
The road climbed gently, winding around the terraced slopes of the Judean hill country. Jesus pointed toward the eastern horizon and said:

"Look at those hills. East of these ridges, Joshua led our fathers across the Jordan Valley, inaugurating the conquest of the Promised Land. Know that all of that triumph was pointing toward something immeasurably greater."
**11. Joshua - The Name that Saves (Joshua 1, 5, 24)**
And he continued:

"After Moses died, the Lord raised up Joshua to bring the work to its culmination—to lead the people into the Promised Land, into the rest that God had prepared for them. And observe his name with utmost care: *Yehoshua*—which means *'The LORD saves'*. It is the very same name that, in its shortened form, you speak every single day whenever you mention the name of... well, you know of whom we are speaking![EN_REF:20]
"The Lord promised Joshua:
*"As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will never leave you nor forsake you."* [Jos 1:5]

"And Joshua fulfilled his calling—he conquered the land, apportioned the inheritance among the tribes, and settled Israel in their rest. Just as Moses was called the servant of the Lord (*'ebed Yahweh*), so Joshua received that very same title when he drew his final breath [Jos 24:29].

"Yet there was an extraordinary encounter you must never forget. On the eve of the fall of Jericho, Joshua looked up and saw a man standing before him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went up to him and asked, *'Are you for us or for our enemies?'*. And the reply was striking:
*"'Neither,' he replied, 'but as commander of the army of the LORD I have now come.'... 'Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.'"* [Jos 5:14-15]

"The very words spoken to Moses at the burning bush! That Commander of the heavenly host—who could he be, if not the Lord himself, appearing in visible form to lead the battle in person? The true Conqueror of Israel was not Joshua—it was the Lord of Hosts.[EN_REF:21]

"Joshua prefigured the Messiah in every way: in the name he bore, in the victory he secured, in the rest he provided, and in the title he inherited. Yet Joshua died, and the rest he gave was earthly and temporary. There had to come another Joshua—another *Yehoshua*—who would bestow upon the people of God true and everlasting rest."
**12. The Judges - The Cry for the Coming King (Judges 2, 17, 21)**

"Yet after Joshua and that entire generation had gathered to their fathers, there followed the darkest chapter in the history of Israel. The people abandoned the Lord, worshipped the idols of surrounding nations, and aroused the holy anger of God. What happened? The Lord gave Israel over into the hands of their enemies. In their misery the people cried out, and God, in sovereign mercy, raised up judges—temporary deliverers—to rescue them. But no sooner had the judge died than Israel returned to corruption, and the tragic cycle began anew.[EN_REF:22]
"A heartbreaking, unrelenting cycle: sin, oppression, weeping, deliverance, and renewed rebellion. And do you know why that spiral never ceased? The book of Judges itself provides the answer:
*"In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit."* [Jdg 21:25]

"Understand: the message of Scripture is clear. Israel needed a king! Not a temporary ruler, not a mortal deliverer whose breath departs—but an enduring, righteous, faithful King who would shepherd the people forever in the ways of the Lord. But we will speak more of the promise of the Messiah in the era of the Kings in just a moment.[EN_REF:23]

"Even in that dark epoch, the Lord did not abandon his covenant people. The Angel of the Lord appeared—first to admonish Israel that he would never break his covenant [Jdg 2:1-5], and later to Manoah's wife, announcing the conception of a deliverer consecrated to God from birth, Samson [Jdg 13:1-5]. That Angel—the Mediator of the covenant—was the living pledge that Israel and the seed of promise would be preserved even in days of deepest apostasy.

"The judges, including Samson, were shadows of the Messiah: each was a deliverer raised up by God to rescue his people. Yet none could remain forever. In every generation, Israel cried out for a new savior. That deep longing—that desperate need—could be answered only by the Savior who would never die."
**13. Hannah's Song - The First Prophecy of the Anointed (1 Samuel 2:1-10)**

"Then, in the darkest hour of the priesthood—when Eli was old and his sons defiled the sanctuary—a barren woman named Hannah poured out her soul in tears before the Lord, pleading for a son. And the Lord heard her. Samuel was born, and Hannah sang a hymn of praise that stands as one of the most sublime messianic prophecies in all the Scriptures.

"Hannah was a humble woman, yet the Spirit of God clothed her as a prophetess. She sang of the God who humbles the proud and exalts the lowly, who kills and brings to life, who raises the poor from the dust to seat them with princes. And then, at the climax of her song, she looked down the corridor of the ages and proclaimed:
*"The LORD will judge the ends of the earth. He will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed."* [1 Sm 2:10]

"Give your closest attention to this title: *his Anointed*—in Hebrew, *Meshiho*—his Messiah! This is the very first time in all the Holy Scriptures that the word 'Messiah'—Anointed One—is used in a prophetic context to designate the coming Sovereign![EN_REF:24]

"Hannah was barren, and God gave her a son. Many centuries later, another humble woman, Mary, the mother of the Messiah, would sing: *'My soul glorifies the Lord... for the Mighty One has done great things for me'*. Hannah's hymn and Mary's Magnificat stand as two sacred mirrors—one looking forward in prophecy, the other celebrating its glorious fulfillment."[EN_REF:25]
**14. Samuel - Prophet, Priest, and Judge (1 Samuel 3, 7, 16)**

"Hannah's son—Samuel—grew up to become a singular figure in the history of Israel. He functioned simultaneously as prophet, priest, and judge. He is the only man in all Scripture who held all three sacred offices at once.[EN_REF:26]

"As a prophet, Samuel initiated the enduring prophetic succession following Moses with unanimous national recognition. All the people acknowledged it: *"And all Israel... recognized that Samuel was attested as a prophet of the LORD"* [1 Sm 3:20]. The word of God was once again revealed through his mouth.

"As a judge, Samuel governed Israel with spotless integrity, traveling year after year on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah [1 Sm 7:15-17]. He was the last of the judges, the living bridge between the era of covenant deliverers and the dawn of the monarchy.

"As a priest, he ministered during the collapse of Eli's house, serving before the Lord from his boyhood and offering sacrifices on behalf of the people. Through him, God's promise to raise up a 'faithful priest' who would act according to his heart began to unfold. He built an altar at Ramah and offered sacrifices, continually interceding for Israel before God [1 Sm 7:17].

"And it was Samuel whom God commissioned to anoint the first two kings of Israel. In his person, all three callings converged, beautifully foreshadowing the One who would come as the supreme Prophet, the eternal High Priest, and the King of kings."[EN_REF:27]
**15. Saul - The Anointed Who Failed (1 Samuel 10, 13, 15)**

"When the people demanded an earthly ruler, clamoring, *'Appoint a king to lead us, such as all the other nations have'* [1 Sm 8:5-6], the Lord told Samuel: *'Listen to all that the people are saying to you; it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected me as their king'* [1 Sm 8:7]. Granting their request in divine forbearance, God selected Saul—tall, handsome, and imposing. Samuel poured the flask of oil over his head and anointed him, saying:
*"Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over his inheritance?"* [1 Sm 10:1]

"Saul was Israel's first anointed king—the first *Mashiach*. He was endowed with royal dignity and given the word of the Lord to guide his path. Yet Saul failed. He presumptuously usurped the priestly office by offering burnt offerings without authorization [1 Sm 13:8-14], blatantly disobeyed the command to destroy Amalek [1 Sm 15:1-24], and succumbed to pride, jealous rage, and bitter stubbornness.[EN_REF:28]
"And Samuel declared to him with solemn finality:
*"You have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you as king over Israel!"* [1 Sm 15:26]

"Consider this deeply: the very first anointed king of Israel was rejected by God. Saul showed the world everything a true Messiah must never be: disobedient, self-reliant, arrogant, and worldly. Yet Saul's failure did not derail God's sovereign plan; rather, it proved that no merely human king could ever fulfill the eternal messianic calling. There was need for a different kind of heart—a man after God's own heart."[EN_REF:29]
**16. David - The Shepherd Who Became King (1 Samuel 16; 2 Samuel 5; 2 Samuel 23:1-5)**
"While Saul still sat upon the throne, the Lord had already chosen his successor. He said to Samuel:
*"Fill your horn with oil and be on your way; I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem. I have chosen one of his sons to be king."* [1 Sm 16:1]

"And Samuel went. Jesse paraded his sons before him—seven fine, strong, impressive young men. Yet of none of them did the Lord say, *'This is the one'*. Until Samuel asked, *'Are these all the sons you have?'*. And Jesse replied that the youngest was still out in the fields, tending the sheep. They sent for him at once.
*"So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day on the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon David."* [1 Sm 16:13]

"The youngest! A shepherd boy! The one whom no one even thought to invite to the feast! Thus works the Lord—he does not look as man looks. *'The LORD does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart'* [1 Sm 16:7].[EN_REF:30]

"And David grew, defeated the giant Goliath in the Valley of Elah, fled from the jealous wrath of Saul, and endured years of hardship in the wilderness, yet he never raised his hand against the Lord's anointed. And when at last he was crowned king in Jerusalem over all Israel, he knew full well where his authority originated.
"Near the close of his earthly pilgrimage, David uttered his last words as a prophetic oracle:

*"The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; his word was on my tongue. The God of Israel spoke, the Rock of Israel said to me: 'When one rules over people in righteousness, when he rules in the fear of God, he is like the light of morning at sunrise on a cloudless morning, like the brightness after rain that brings grass from the earth.'"* [2 Sm 23:2-4]
"And then David added with unshakeable faith:
*"If my house were not right with God, surely he would not have made with me an everlasting covenant, arranged and secured in every part."* [2 Sm 23:5]

"David recognized himself as *'the anointed of the God of Jacob'* (*meshîah 'elohê ya'aqob*) [2 Sm 23:1], and he prophesied that from his line would arise the righteous, God-fearing Sovereign whose blessing would be like the radiant morning sun and life-giving rain upon the earth. David was the first firm foundation, but the ultimate fulfillment—as we shall see—belonged to an everlasting glory."[EN_REF:31]
**17. The Covenant with David - An Eternal Throne (2 Samuel 7:12-16)**

"And now we come to the very heart of the history of the kings. When David desired to build a house for the Lord—a permanent temple for the ark of the covenant—the prophet Nathan brought him the word of the Most High. And what an astonishing word it was!

"The Lord said in essence: *'Would you build a house for me? NO—I will build a house for you!'*. Yet the 'house' God promised was not framed with stone and cedar; it was an everlasting dynasty, an eternal royal line:

*"When your days are over and you rest with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, your own flesh and blood, and I will establish his kingdom. He is the one who will build a house for my Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he will be my son."* [2 Sm 7:12-14][EN_REF:32]
"And the divine promise continues:
*"Your house and your kingdom will endure forever before me; your throne will be established forever."* [2 Sm 7:16]

"Three times the words *'forever'* ring out! And God swears a unique, intimate bond: *'I will be his father, and he will be my son'*. Not mere legal adoption, but a relationship of divine sonship.[EN_REF:33]

"Friends, Solomon built the earthly temple, yet Solomon fell into sin and died. The kingdom fractured. The kings of Judah, one after another, faltered and failed. The Temple was burned to ashes by Babylon, and the throne of David seemed lost to history. Yet the Word of God never returns void! The promise of an eternal kingdom can be fulfilled only by a King who neither sins nor dies—the true Son of God in the fullest sense.
"And David grasped this truth with awe. When he received this promise, he sat before the Lord in worship and prayed:

*"Who am I, Sovereign LORD, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far? And as if this were not enough in your sight, Sovereign LORD, you have also spoken about the future of the house of your servant."* [2 Sm 7:18-19]

"Far into the distant future—David knew this promise looked far beyond Solomon, far beyond any mortal king. That covenant would span the centuries until reaching its final fulfillment in the Offspring of David who would be, at the same time, the Son of God."[EN_REF:34]
**PART III - THE PSALMS - POETIC ELABORATION OF THE MESSIANIC HOPE**
The pathway now climbed across a steeper ridge, framed by limestone outcroppings and scattered wild olive trees.

As the Traveler unfolded the sacred testimonies of the Torah and the Former Prophets, the two disciples exchanged silent, wondering glances. The hesitant reserve they had initially maintained toward this stranger was melting away like morning mist upon the road. Feeling an inexplicable, burning warmth comforting their chests, Cleopas leaned gently toward their Companion and spoke with the trembling voice of one beginning to glimpse something glorious: —"Sir, you speak of these prophecies with a luminous clarity and an authority we have never heard among the doctors of the Law in Jerusalem... Did you happen to know Master Jesus personally, or were you with him before the Passover?"

Their Master smiled tenderly and told them that true understanding of the Scriptures is granted only when one sees that they bear witness of the Messiah; and that if the heart is opened to the heavenly revelation from above, they will no longer walk in darkness, for all who know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God fall into tragic error...
Now Jesus prepared to quote the Psalms from memory, as One who had sung them countless times, or as One who was eternally present when the sacred bards inscribed them upon parchment.
**18. The Psalm of the Anointed - The Messiah Declared Son of God (Psalm 2)**
"Listen, my friends, to what David sang:
*"Why do the nations conspire and the peoples plot in vain? The kings of the earth rise up and the rulers band together against the LORD and against his anointed."* [Ps 2:1-2]

"Against his Anointed—against his Messiah! The nations rose up against him. The rulers conspired against him. And you saw this fulfilled with your very eyes only three days ago. The chief priests, the scribes of the Sanhedrin, Pontius Pilate, Herod—all aligned themselves against the Lord's Anointed.
"Yet hear what the Lord declares in answer:
*"'I have installed my king on Zion, my holy mountain.' I will proclaim the LORD's decree: He said to me, 'You are my son; today I have become your father.'"* [Ps 2:6-7]
"And hear the promise of the Father:
*"Ask me, and I will make the nations your inheritance, the ends of the earth your possession."* [Ps 2:8]
"The Messiah is proclaimed the only begotten Son of God. He reigns now not over the hills of Judea alone, but over all the nations of the earth. And blessed are all who take refuge in him!"
**19. The Psalm of Agony - My God, Why Have You Forsaken Me? (Psalm 22)**
"Yet the Messiah's pathway to his triumphant throne leads first through the valley of the shadow of death. David sang a prophetic psalm that could never be confined to his own personal trials:
*"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"* [Ps 22:1]
*"All who see me mock me; they hurl insults, shaking their heads. 'He trusts in the LORD,' they say, 'let the LORD rescue him. Let him deliver him, since he delights in him.'"* [Ps 22:7-8][EN_REF:35]

*"Dogs surround me, a pack of villains encircles me; they pierce my hands and my feet. All my bones are on display; people stare and gloat over me. They divide my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment."* [Ps 22:16-18]

"Friends, you beheld every single one of those words take place three days ago at Golgotha. The mocking onlookers, the Roman nails piercing hands and feet, the soldiers casting lots for his seamless tunic. Yet the psalm does not conclude in the grave! It breaks forth into boundless victory:

*"All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD, and all the families of the nations will bow down before him, for dominion belongs to the LORD and he rules over the nations."* [Ps 22:27-28]
"Understand that the suffering of the Messiah was never a mark of defeat—it was the sovereign pathway ordained by God to awaken the universal worship of all nations!"[EN_REF:36]
**20. The Eternal Throne - Your Throne, O God, Endures Forever (Psalm 45)**
"In the royal wedding hymns of Israel, the psalmist lifted his voice in a song of praise echoing down through the centuries, celebrating the deity and majesty of Him who shall reign forever:

*"Your throne, O God, will last for ever and ever; a scepter of justice will be the scepter of your kingdom. You love righteousness and hate wickedness; therefore God, your God, has set you above your companions by anointing you with the oil of joy."* [Ps 45:6-7][EN_REF:37]

"Notice that the psalmist addresses the King as *'O God!'*! This is no ordinary mortal monarch. This is the divine King—the Anointed One who is both truly human and truly God, reigning with eternal righteousness."
**21. The King of Righteousness and Universal Peace (Psalm 72)**
"And Solomon prayed for the coming of a celestial kingdom far exceeding his own earthly glory:

*"May he judge your people in righteousness, your afflicted ones with justice... May he be like rain falling on a mown field, like showers watering the earth. In his days may the righteous flourish and prosperity abound till the moon is no more. May he rule from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth... May all kings bow down to him and all nations serve him."* [Ps 72:2, 6-8, 11]

"All nations! A dominion expanding from sea to sea! An era of righteous peace enduring as long as the sun and the moon shine! This does not speak of Solomon, my friends—it speaks of One who is greater than Solomon."[EN_REF:38]
**22. A Priest Forever - In the Order of Melchizedek (Psalm 110)**
"And listen to the most extraordinary revelation given to King David. The Lord spoke to the Messiah—not as to a servant, but as to his Lord:
*"The LORD says to my lord: 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.'"* [Ps 110:1]

"David calls the Messiah *'my Lord'*. How can the Messiah be at once David's descendant according to the flesh, and David's divine Lord? There is only one answer: he is both human—of David's royal seed—and divine—the eternal Lord.[EN_REF:39]
"And the divine oath continues:
*"The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind: 'You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek.'"* [Ps 110:4]

"The Messiah is not only King. He is also Priest—yet not in the passing order of Aaron, whose priests died and were replaced from generation to generation. He is Priest in the eternal order of Melchizedek: having neither beginning of days nor end of life. An everlasting Priest over an everlasting Kingdom![EN_REF:40]

"Levitical priests offered daily, repetitive sacrifices that could never take away sins. The Messiah, however, offered one single, all-sufficient sacrifice for all time, seating himself at the right hand of the Majesty on high as our eternal High Priest and sovereign King."
**23. The Rejected Stone (Psalm 118:22-23)**
"And the builders—the religious leaders of Israel—would despise and cast aside the chief stone:
*"The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; the LORD has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes."* [Ps 118:22-23]

"The rejected stone... you saw it happen with breaking hearts. He was rejected by the chief priests, by the elders, by the Sanhedrin. Yet that very stone cast away by men has been exalted by God as the Cornerstone—the chief cornerstone of the entire temple of redemption."
**PART IV - THE LATTER PROPHETS**

The sun was now resting upon the crest of the western hills of Emmaus, hanging low on the horizon and painting the sky in deep amber, crimson, and violet hues. A fresh evening breeze began to stir from the mountain passes. The fine chalk dust of the road, kicked up by their sandals, hung suspended in the golden evening light.
Jesus was now approaching the climax of his discourse, having illuminated the hidden treasures of the Pentateuch and the Sacred Poetry. Yet there remained the burning visions of the Prophets.
Though radiating unshakeable peace, his voice now carried a solemn, compelling urgency.

The gaze of the two disciples was torn between the fading splendor of the twilight road and the overwhelming presence of this mysterious traveler. Their faces, once sunken in grief and confusion, now shone with breathless wonder and reverent fascination. It was hard to tell whether they were breathless from the steep ascent or from the fire blazing within their souls.
Nathaniel leaned over and whispered into Cleopas's ear:

"Cleopas... who is this man? He no longer seems a stranger to me. He does not speak like the pilgrims who journey through Judea, nor like the scribes of Jerusalem. When he explains the Scriptures, he does not merely recall dead words—he speaks as though he stood present at the very hour when those eternal covenants were ratified! Do you not feel the very same fire burning in your chest as he walks with us?"
**24. Isaiah - The Virgin's Son - Immanuel (Isaiah 7:14)**
Then Jesus continued:

"Listen now to Isaiah, the prince of the prophets. When King Ahaz trembled in fear before the allied armies of Syria and Ephraim, the Lord offered him a miraculous sign—any sign, whether in the deepest depths or the highest heavens. Ahaz, in false piety, refused. Then Isaiah declared, centuries before the Messiah's birth:
*"Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel."* [Is 7:14]

"A Son born of a virgin! And his name would be Immanuel—meaning *'God with us'*. God would not remain distant in the heavenly heights: he would come down to dwell with us in person, clothed in human flesh."[EN_REF:41]
**25. Isaiah - The Child Who Reigns - Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6-7)**
"And Isaiah saw even further. He beheld that this Son would be no ordinary ruler:

*"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Of the greatness of his government and peace there will be no end. He will reign on David's throne and over his kingdom, establishing and upholding it with justice and righteousness from that time on and forever."* [Is 9:6-7]

"Look closely at the divine titles Isaiah gives this child: Mighty God! Everlasting Father! This child born of woman is at once true man and bearer of the majesty of Almighty God. He shall sit upon David's throne—fulfilling the eternal covenant spoken through Nathan. And of his reign and of his peace there will never be an end."[EN_REF:42]
**26. Isaiah - The Root of Jesse (Isaiah 11:1-10)**
"And Isaiah saw the Messiah spring forth—not from a proud cedar, but from a felled stump:

*"A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse; from his roots a Branch will bear fruit. The Spirit of the LORD will rest on him— the Spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the Spirit of counsel and of might, the Spirit of the knowledge and fear of the LORD."* [Is 11:1-2]

"The stump of Jesse—the royal line of David—would be cut down. The earthly monarchy would fall into ruin. Yet from its roots, from an apparently lifeless stump, a living Branch would blossom. The sevenfold fullness of the Spirit of the Lord would rest upon him, spreading the knowledge of God across the world:
*"For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea."* [Is 11:9]

"And he would rule in righteousness, establishing the Kingdom of Heaven that—believe me—has already begun in power, experienced by you even now until its glorious consummation, when every creature under heaven acknowledges that Jesus reigns and shall return in glory.
**27. Isaiah - The Four Servant Songs (Isaiah 42, 49, 50, 52-53)**

"Now we arrive at that which has proven hardest for your hearts to embrace, yet which is the most vital of all. Isaiah spoke of a Servant of the Lord—a Servant who would accomplish a redemptive work that no king, priest, or prophet before him could ever achieve.
"In the First Song, the Servant is presented:

*"Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom I delight; I will put my Spirit on him, and he will bring justice to the nations. He will not shout or cry out, or raise his voice in the streets. A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out. In faithfulness he will bring forth justice."* [Is 42:1-3]
"In the Second Song, the Servant is consecrated from his mother's womb:

*"Before I was born the LORD called me; from my mother's womb he has spoken my name... 'It is too small a thing for you to be my servant to restore the tribes of Jacob... I will also make you a light for the Gentiles, that my salvation may reach to the ends of the earth.'"* [Is 49:1, 6]
"In the Third Song, the Servant willingly yields his body to shame:
*"I offered my back to those who beat me, my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard; I did not hide my face from mocking and spitting."* [Is 50:6]
"And in the Fourth Song, the Servant suffers, atones, and dies for our sins.
"Listen now with quiet reverence. These are the sacred words that explain everything that has transpired in Jerusalem these past days:
*"See, my servant will act wisely; he will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted."* [Is 52:13]
*"He was despised and rejected by mankind, a man of suffering, and familiar with pain... and we held him in low esteem."* [Is 53:3]
*"Surely he took up our pain and bore our suffering, yet we considered him punished by God, stricken by him, and afflicted."* [Is 53:4]
*"But he was pierced for our transgressions, he was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we are healed."* [Is 53:5]
*"We all, like sheep, have gone astray, each of us has turned to our own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all."* [Is 53:6]
*"He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; he was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth."* [Is 53:7]
*"He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence, nor was any deceit in his mouth."* [Is 53:9]

*"Yet it was the LORD's will to crush him and cause him to suffer, and though the LORD makes his life an offering for sin, he will see his offspring and prolong his days, and the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand."* [Is 53:10]
*"After he has suffered, he will see the light of life and be satisfied; by his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities."* [Is 53:11]

"Friends, do you hear the voice of Isaiah? His prophecy affirms that the Messiah, the Righteous One, was wounded for our transgressions. I repeat: for our transgressions—not his own! The Lord laid upon him the iniquity of us all. There was no deceit found in his mouth, yet it pleased the Father to crush him, rendering his life an offering for sin. He was the ultimate sacrifice: the true Passover Lamb, the scapegoat of the Day of Atonement, the guilt offering—not an animal, but a Man: the Servant of the Lord.

"It was necessary that the Messiah should suffer these things—not by tragic misfortune, not in defeat, but according to the eternal purpose of God. The death of the Messiah is the propitiation for the sins of the world! And behold: Isaiah declares that *'he will see his offspring'* and *'prolong his days'*. After laying down his life as an offering for sin... can a man behold his offspring after death, unless... he rises again from the dead?"[EN_REF:43]
**28. Isaiah - Anointed to Proclaim Good News (Isaiah 61:1-3)**
"And Isaiah foretold the public ministry of the Servant:

*"The Spirit of the Sovereign LORD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom for the captives and release from darkness for the prisoners, to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn."* [Is 61:1-2]

"The Messiah was not to come merely as a political conqueror. He was to come first as a preacher of good tidings, a healer of the brokenhearted, a deliverer—not primarily from Roman or Greek legions, but from the eternal tyranny of sin and death."

Cleopas halted in the middle of the road, wiping the dust and sweat from his forehead with the sleeve of his cloak, and looked upon their Traveling Companion with eyes filled with tears. The sharp edge of grief had yielded to an unutterable peace. With a voice shaking with emotion, he gently interrupted him:

"How can this be? As you speak, the crushing ache in our hearts simply vanishes away. It is as if every passage of the Law and the Prophets, which once seemed hidden behind a heavy veil of shadows, has suddenly burst into living light pointing to a single face!"
**29. Jeremiah - The Righteous Branch and the New Covenant (Jeremiah 23:5-6; 31:31-34)**
"Yes, Cleopas!" said Jesus with infinite tenderness. "The Word of God comforts and transforms the human heart."
And he continued concerning the prophets of the Lord:

"And what of Jeremiah, who witnessed the destruction of Jerusalem? Did he not prophesy that out of the house of David the Lord would raise up a King who would reign wisely and execute justice? Hear what is written:

*"'The days are coming,' declares the LORD, 'when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, a King who will reign wisely and do what is just and right in the land. In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will live in safety. This is the name by which he will be called: The LORD Our Righteous Savior.'"* [Jr 23:5-6]
"The name of the Branch is *'The LORD Our Righteousness'*—Yahweh Tsidkenu! The Messiah bears the very name of the living God!
"And Jeremiah prophesied something even more magnificent—a new covenant:

*"'The days are coming,' declares the LORD, 'when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and with the people of Judah... I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people... For I will forgive their wickedness and will remember their sins no more.'"* [Jr 31:31, 33-34]
"A new covenant! Inscribed not on tablets of stone, but upon the living tablets of the heart. And the foundation of this covenant, understand, is the full and everlasting forgiveness of sins."
**30. Ezekiel - The Shepherd of Israel (Ezekiel 34:23-24; 37:24-25)**
"Ezekiel, in exile by the Kebar River, heard the Lord promise a Shepherd:

*"I will place over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he will tend them; he will tend them and be their shepherd. I the LORD will be their God, and my servant David will be prince among them."* [Ez 34:23-24]
*"'My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd.'"* [Ez 37:24]

"God called this prince *'My servant David'*. But how could that be, when King David had been dead for centuries? The meaning is unmistakably clear: Ezekiel speaks of David's royal Descendant—the Messiah—who is the true Shepherd of Israel, tending his flock in righteousness and peace."
**31. Daniel - The Son of Man and the Seventy Weeks (Daniel 7:13-14; 9:24-27)**
"And what of Daniel, who received astonishing apocalyptic visions in Babylon?[EN_REF:44]
"In his first vision, he beheld the empires of the earth rise and fall—Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome—and then:

*"In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence. He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshiped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed."* [Dn 7:13-14]

"The Son of Man—a heavenly, divine figure who comes upon the clouds of heaven and receives worship and everlasting dominion over every nation! Not a fragile political dynasty, but a Kingdom that shall never be overthrown.
"And in the second vision, Daniel was given the exact prophetic timeline for the coming of the Messiah:

*"Seventy 'sevens' are decreed for your people and your holy city to finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for wickedness, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy and to anoint the Most Holy Place."* [Dn 9:24]

*"Know and understand this: From the time the word goes out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the ruler, comes, there will be seven 'sevens,' and sixty-two 'sevens.'... After the sixty-two 'sevens,' the Anointed One will be put to death and will have nothing."* [Dn 9:25-26]

*'The Anointed One will be cut off'*, he will be put to death! Daniel prophesied that the Messiah would come, make an end of sins, atone for iniquity—and be slain! Do not be confounded, for you know the Scriptures. This was his sacred mission."
**32. The Sign of Jonah - Three Days and Three Nights (Jonah 1-2)**
Jesus paused. He looked upon the two disciples with gentle compassion, allowing a moment of quiet reflection, and then continued:
"Recall the prophet Jonah. When the rulers of Israel demanded a sign from heaven, what were they told? That no sign would be given them except the sign of the prophet Jonah. And what was that sign?

"To quiet the raging sea and save the sailors on board, Jonah offered himself as a sacrifice: *'Pick me up and throw me into the sea,' he replied, 'and it will become calm'* [Jon 1:12]. He knew that the death of one would save the many. The tempest of God's wrath subsided when the prophet was swallowed by the deep.
*"Now the LORD provided a huge fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights."* [Jon 1:17]
"Friends, in his agony, Jonah prayed that he had cried out from the depths of Sheol—sinking down to the roots of the mountains, the bars of the earth closing over him forever [Jon 2:2, 6].
"Jonah was, in figure, dead. Yet on the third day, the Lord commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land [Jon 2:10].

"Just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so it was necessary for the Son of Man to be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth! But the tomb could not hold him. The resurrection on the third day announced to you by the women this morning is the supreme sign of God!

"And consider what followed: Jonah went and preached to the great city of Nineveh, a heathen nation of pagans, and they repented in dust and ashes. I tell you solemnly: the death and resurrection of the Messiah open wide the gates of salvation, not to the Jews alone, but to every nation upon the earth!"[EN_REF:45]
**33. Micah - The Ruler Born in Bethlehem (Micah 5:2)**
"Let us not forget Micah, the prophet who pinpointed the very village where the Messiah was to be born:

*"But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times... He will stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. And they will live securely, for then his greatness will reach to the ends of the earth. And he will be our peace."* [Mic 5:2, 4-5]

"Behold! A ruler promised from of old, whose birthplace according to the Scriptures was Bethlehem, the city of David. Yet at the same time, as we have seen, he is the pre-existent, eternal King from everlasting!"[EN_REF:46]
**34. Haggai - The Greater Glory of the Second Temple (Haggai 2:6-9)**
"Remember how, when the exiles returned and rebuilt the Temple, the elders wept because it seemed so meager compared to Solomon's splendor? Yet the Lord spoke through Haggai:

*"This is what the LORD Almighty says: 'In a little while I will once more shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land. I will shake all nations, and what is desired by all nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory... The glory of this present house will be greater than the glory of the former house.'"* [Hg 2:6-9]

"The Desire of all nations promised to visit and fill that house with glory! The glory of the second Temple would surpass that of Solomon—not in gold or silver, but because the Messiah himself would enter its courts and proclaim spiritual riches to you! Believe it!"[EN_REF:47]
**35. Zechariah - The Humble King, Thirty Pieces of Silver, and the Pierced One (Zechariah 9-13)**
"And Zechariah? Ah, Zechariah saw everything with astonishing, piercing clarity!
"He beheld the King entering Jerusalem:
*"Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! Shout, Daughter Jerusalem! See, your king comes to you, righteous and victorious, lowly and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey."* [Zec 9:9]
"You saw this take place only a week ago! He entered Jerusalem riding upon a colt, while the crowds carpeted the road with palm branches, shouting *'Hosanna to the Son of David!'*.
"Moreover, when Zechariah served as a shepherd rejected by his own flock, he saw the exact price of betrayal:

*"I told them, 'If you think it best, give me my pay; but if not, keep it.' So they paid me thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said to me, 'Throw it to the potter'—the handsome price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter at the house of the LORD."* [Zec 11:12-13]
"Thirty pieces of silver! The exact valuation of a common slave! The exact price paid for the betrayal of Jesus Christ by Judas Iscariot![EN_REF:48]
"And Zechariah foresaw that most solemn and terrible hour upon the hill of crucifixion:

*"And I will pour out on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication. They will look on me, the one they have pierced, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for him as one grieves for a firstborn son."* [Zec 12:10]

*'They will look on me, the one they have pierced!'* It is the Lord who speaks! He declares that he himself would be pierced—and that the people would gaze upon him with bitter mourning! And then God reveals:
*"On that day a fountain will be opened to the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity."* [Zec 13:1]
"From the pierced side of the Savior flows an open fountain of cleansing for all the sin and impurity of Israel!"[EN_REF:49]
**36. Malachi - The Messenger of the Covenant and the Sun of Righteousness (Malachi 3:1; 4:5-6)**
"And listen now to the final prophetic voice of the Old Testament. Malachi, the seal of the prophets, proclaimed:

*"'I will send my messenger, who will prepare the way before me. Then suddenly the Lord you are seeking will come to his temple; the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, will come,' says the LORD Almighty."* [Mal 3:1]
"First would come a messenger—to prepare the way. And immediately following, the Lord himself would enter his temple: the Messenger of the Covenant, the Messiah!
"And Malachi closed the revelation of the Old Testament with these timeless words:

*"See, I will send the prophet Elijah to you before that great and dreadful day of the LORD comes. He will turn the hearts of the parents to their children, and the hearts of the children to their parents."* [Mal 4:5-6]

"You know who that new Elijah was: John, the son of Zechariah, who baptized in the Jordan and pointed to the One coming after him, crying: *'Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!'*"[EN_REF:50]
**PART V - "WAS IT NOT NECESSARY?"**

The village of Emmaus now appeared ahead of the travelers, bathed in the tender golden glow of the setting sun. The Traveler, Jesus, made as if he were going farther, continuing past the village along the ascending road, but Cleopas stepped forward and gently laid hold of the Master's cloak.
With a voice shaking with the urgency of one whose hope had been miraculously reborn from the ashes of despair, he pleaded:

"Lord, stay with us! It is nearly evening; the day is almost over, and darkness will soon envelope the roads of Judea. Do not leave us now, for your words have brought heaven's light to our souls. Come in, break bread at our table!"
Jesus consented. And as he poured water from a clay pitcher at the threshold to wash the road dust from his feet, he concluded:

"You asked me why the Messiah had to suffer. Now you hold heaven's answer. All the Scriptures bear witness of him—from the seed of the woman in the garden of Eden to the Lamb of God proclaimed by John the Baptist. From the covenant promise given to Abraham to the new covenant written upon the heart in Jeremiah. From the everlasting throne sworn to David to the heavenly Son of Man seen by Daniel.
"From the bronze serpent lifted high in the wilderness to the Servant of Isaiah, pierced through for our transgressions.
*"Did not the Messiah have to suffer these things and then enter his glory?"* [Lk 24:26]

"The suffering of Jesus Christ was never a defeat of God's redemptive purpose—it was the very purpose of God fulfilled. The cross was not the end—it was the holy altar whereby the divine Lamb took away the sin of the world; whereby the seed of the woman crushed the serpent's head; whereby the Priest in the order of Melchizedek offered the one all-sufficient sacrifice; and whereby the King of kings inaugurated his eternal Kingdom."
Entering the simple dwelling, Cleopas set the oil lamp upon the table and, gazing intently into the face of their Traveler with tears of joy, whispered:

"Lord, the bitter grief we carried as we fled Jerusalem has vanished along the road. Your words have breathed life back into our souls. Sit with us; the bread is set, and we cannot bear for this fellowship to end."
*"When he was at the table with them, he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and began to give it to them. Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him, and he disappeared from their sight.*
*They asked each other, 'Were not our hearts burning within us while he talked with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?'"*
